replacements.c009: Although science is increasingly specialized, solving problems requires scientists to combine knowledge from chemistry and physics.
replacements.c012: High school students should study broadly to prepare for university learning.

replacements.c009: Science is becoming more specialized, yet scientists must draw on both chemistry and physics to solve problems.
replacements.c012: By learning across disciplines, high school students can prepare themselves for future study at university.

replacements.c005: Work and family pressures often force adults to give up lifelong hobbies.
replacements.c006: Consequently, they cannot devote as much time and effort to favorite games as they did 15 or 20 years earlier.

replacements.c005: The demands of employment and family life frequently lead adults to abandon hobbies they have enjoyed for years.
replacements.c006: As a result, they lack the time and energy to pursue their favorite games as they once did, 15 or 20 years ago.

replacements.c003: Governments can build more housing rather than preserve old buildings.
replacements.c005: Rapid urbanization, as rural residents move to cities for jobs, has made preserving old buildings more urgent.

replacements.c003: Instead of conserving old buildings, governments could use the space to provide additional accommodation.
replacements.c005: The preservation issue has grown more pressing as rapid urbanization sends rural people to urban centers in search of work.
Governments should help citizens learn to prevent illnesses that could cause suffering.
replacements.c007: A Turkish Ministry of Health campaign targeting youth smoking improved the well-being and lifestyles of those who quit.

replacements.c005: One governmental responsibility is to give citizens the means to learn how to avoid illnesses that may bring misery to their lives.
replacements.c007: For example, a Turkish Ministry of Health campaign against youth smoking helped those who stopped to live more healthily and enjoy greater well-being.
